newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields ease at close, bill futures outperform.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields ease at close, bill futures outperform.

* NZ bank bill, bond yields consolidate lower
* Movement mostly currency related
* Bill futures actively traded
New Zealand bank bill and bond yields ended slightly lower on Tuesday in line with a slightly stronger currency.
Trade was light except for bank bill futures, the June contract ending six points higher at 92.98 on 2,573 lots.
In the physical market, yields eased a few basis points.
"I guess it was just a consolidation of the recent positive tone we've had in New Zealand," said one Wellington dealer. "Certainly the currency is not doing it any harm," he said.
Future direction was expected to be set by overseas markets after holidays in the United States and Britain on Monday.
One other dealer said there was little or no reaction to PPI data, which showed producer price inflation for inputs rose just 0.1 percent over the year to March.
Rather, he said the action in the bill futures was in response to rumours of more eurokiwi issuance.
"With the strength in the TWI, you've seen the bill futures continuing to rally. I think that probably triggered a few stops," he said.
The bill curve had become flatter, with a little buying in the six to 12 months on the belief that the Reserve Bank's June 27 statement would be more positive than previously thought.
"At the end of the day, it's very much driven by the TWI and the view that inflation is not as big a concern as what it once was six months ago," he said.
